title: Time: 12-Hour and 24-Hour Time, Calendars and Time Intervals
seo_title: Grade 4 Time Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Read, tell and write time in 12-hour and 24-hour formats on both analogue and digital instruments in hours, minutes and seconds; use clocks, calendars and stopwatches; calculate the number of days between dates and time intervals given in whole hours or whole minutes.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 4 time worksheets: analogue and digital clocks, 12-hour and 24-hour time, units of time, time intervals, calendars and timetables. 100 questions with memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • On an analogue clock, the short hand shows the hour and the long hand the minutes.
  • 12-hour time uses a.m. (midnight to noon) and p.m. (noon to midnight). 24-hour time counts from 00:00 to 23:59: 3:15 p.m. = 15:15.
  • 60 seconds = 1 minute, 60 minutes = 1 hour, 24 hours = 1 day, 7 days = 1 week.
  • To find a time interval, count on in hours, then minutes.

Examples

Example

From 08:40 to 11:15

08:40 → 10:40 is 2 hours

10:40 → 11:15 is 35 minutes

Answer: 2 hours 35 minutes

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Hour hand as minutesThe long hand shows the minutes.
Adding 10 for p.m.Add 12: 7 p.m. = 19:00.
Counting the start dateFrom 3 to 10 May is 7 days.

items.q: Write 10 past 9 at night as a 12-hour digital time.
items.e: “10 past 9” means 10 minutes after 9 o’clock: 9:10. At night means pm, so it is 9:10 pm.

items.q: Write 5 to 5 in the afternoon as a 12-hour digital time.
items.e: “5 to 5” means 5 minutes before 5 o’clock. 60 − 5 = 55, so it is 4:55. In the afternoon means pm, so it is 4:55 pm.

items.q: Write 25 to 4 in the afternoon as a 12-hour digital time.
items.e: “25 to 4” means 25 minutes before 4 o’clock. 60 − 25 = 35, so it is 3:35. In the afternoon means pm, so it is 3:35 pm.

items.q: Write quarter to 9 in the morning as a 12-hour digital time.
items.e: “quarter to 9” means 15 minutes before 9 o’clock. 60 − 15 = 45, so it is 8:45. In the morning means am, so it is 8:45 am.

items.q: Write 20 past 7 in the evening as a 12-hour digital time.
items.e: “20 past 7” means 20 minutes after 7 o’clock: 7:20. In the evening means pm, so it is 7:20 pm.

items.q: Write 10 to 12 in the morning as a 12-hour digital time.
items.e: “10 to 12” means 10 minutes before 12 o’clock. 60 − 10 = 50, so it is 11:50. In the morning means am, so it is 11:50 am.

items.q: Which 24-hour time is quarter to 4 in the afternoon?
items.e: “quarter to 4” is 15 minutes before 4 o’clock: 3:45 pm. Add 12 to the hour: 15:45.

items.q: Which 24-hour time is 25 to 4 in the afternoon?
items.e: “25 to 4” is 25 minutes before 4 o’clock: 3:35 pm. Add 12 to the hour: 15:35.

items.q: Which 24-hour time is 20 past 9 in the evening?
items.e: “20 past 9” is 9:20 pm. Add 12 to the hour: 9 + 12 = 21. So it is 21:20.

items.q: How many minutes are in 2 hours?
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 2 × 60 = 120 minutes.

items.q: How many seconds are in 4 minutes?
items.e: 1 minute = 60 seconds. 4 × 60 = 240 seconds.

items.q: How many months are in 6 years?
items.e: 1 year = 12 months. 6 × 12 = 72 months.

items.q: How many days are in 9 weeks?
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. 9 × 7 = 63 days.

12 months make 1 year. 3 × 12 = 36, and 42 − 36 = 6. So 42 months = 3 years 6 months. (Do not split by 10: a year has 12 months.)
7 days make 1 week. 4 × 7 = 28, and 31 − 28 = 3. So 31 days = 4 weeks 3 days.

items.q: How long is it from 11:10 to 11:30?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 30 − 10 = 20 minutes.

items.q: How long is it from 16:20 to 16:45?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 45 − 20 = 25 minutes.

items.q: How long is it from 19:05 to 19:35?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 35 − 5 = 30 minutes.

items.q: How long is it from 14:40 to 15:25?
items.e: Count on to the next hour first: 14:40 to 15:00 is 20 minutes. Then 15:00 to 15:25 is 25 minutes. 20 + 25 = 45 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 08:45 to 09:25?
items.e: Count on to the next hour first: 08:45 to 09:00 is 15 minutes. Then 09:00 to 09:25 is 25 minutes. 15 + 25 = 40 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 11:54 to 12:18?
items.e: Count on to the next hour first: 11:54 to 12:00 is 6 minutes. Then 12:00 to 12:18 is 18 minutes. 6 + 18 = 24 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 12:54 to 13:25?
items.e: Count on to the next hour first: 12:54 to 13:00 is 6 minutes. Then 13:00 to 13:25 is 25 minutes. 6 + 25 = 31 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 17:15 to 18:20?
items.e: Count on to the next hour first: 17:15 to 18:00 is 45 minutes. Then 18:00 to 18:20 is 20 minutes. 45 + 20 = 65 minutes = 1 hour 5 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 11:25 to 12:30?
items.e: Count on to the next hour first: 11:25 to 12:00 is 35 minutes. Then 12:00 to 12:30 is 30 minutes. 35 + 30 = 65 minutes = 1 hour 5 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: How long is it from 14:45 to 16:00?
items.e: Count on to the next hour first: 14:45 to 15:00 is 15 minutes. Then 15:00 to 16:00 is 60 minutes. 15 + 60 = 75 minutes = 1 hour 15 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)
“30 days has September, April, June and November.” So April has 30 days.
September, April, June and November have 30 days. February has 28 (29 in a leap year). All the others, including July, have 31.

items.q: Look at the calendar. What day of the week is 18 March?
items.e: Find 18 in the calendar and go up its column to the top: Thursday.
Leap years come every 4 years. 2 024 was a leap year, so the next one is 2 024 + 4 = 2 028. (2 028 ÷ 4 = 507 with no remainder.)

items.q: 2 028 is a leap year. How many days are in February 2 028?
items.e: February has 28 days, but in a leap year it gets one extra day: 29 days.

items.q: What is the date of the second Saturday in March 2 027?
items.e: The Saturdays are 6, 13, 20, 27. The second one is 13 March. (6 March is the first Saturday and 14 March is a Sunday.)

items.q: Lerato has a swimming lesson every Friday in March. How many lessons is that?
items.e: The Fridays are 5, 12, 19, 26. That is 4 lessons. (Not every month has 5 of each day.)

items.q: What is the date 1 week after Thursday 11 March?
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. 11 + 7 = 18. Go straight down one row on the calendar: Thursday 18 March. (17 March counts 11 March as the first day.)

items.q: What is the date 10 days after 12 March?
items.e: 12 + 10 = 22 March. (21 March counts 12 March as one of the 10 days.)

items.q: How many days is it from 4 March to 19 March?
items.e: 19 − 4 = 15 days. Count the jumps from one day to the next: 5, 6, 7 … 19 is 15 jumps. (16 counts 4 March as well, but no time has passed on the start day.)

items.q: The bus leaves the Bus Station at 16:10. What time does it get to Park Road?
items.e: Find 16:10 in the Bus Station row. Go down that column to the Park Road row: 16:52.

items.q: A bus gets to the Library at 17:37. What time did it leave the Bus Station?
items.e: Find 17:37 in the Library row. Go up that column to the Bus Station row: 17:10.

items.q: How long does the bus that leaves the Bus Station at 16:40 take to get to Park Road?
items.e: 16:40 to 17:00 is 20 minutes. 17:00 to 17:22 is 22 minutes. 20 + 22 = 42 minutes.

items.q: Kabelo must be at Park Road by 17:30. What is the latest bus he can catch from Market Square?
items.e: Look along the Park Road row for the last time that is not after 17:30: 17:22. Go up that column to Market Square: 16:53. The next bus gets to Park Road at 17:52, which is too late.

items.q: Zinhle gets to Market Square at 16:59, just after a bus has left. How long must she wait for the next one?
items.e: The bus at 16:53 has gone. The next bus from Market Square is at 17:23. From 16:59 to 17:23 is 24 minutes.

items.q: Ruan’s bus gets to the Library at 5:07 pm. Which time on the timetable is this?
items.e: 5:07 pm is in the afternoon or evening, so add 12 to the hour: 5 + 12 = 17. Look for 17:07 in the Library row.

items.q: Tea is at 17:30. A pie takes 45 minutes to cook. What time must it go in the oven?
items.e: Count back 30 minutes to 17:00. Then count back 15 more minutes: 16:45.

items.q: A film starts at 18:50 and lasts 1 hour 35 minutes. What time does it finish?
items.e: 18:50 + 1 hour = 19:50. Then add 35 minutes: 10 minutes to 20:00, then 25 more minutes: 20:25.

items.q: Kyle’s holiday lasts 3 weeks 4 days. How many days is that?
items.e: 3 weeks = 3 × 7 = 21 days. 21 + 4 = 25 days.

items.q: Ofentse is 8 years 7 months old. How old is she in months?
items.e: 8 years = 8 × 12 = 96 months. 96 + 7 = 103 months.
